question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit outbound Slack DM recipient policy, and if so should it be Slack-only or a shared message-tool/plugin contract?
rationale: The change adds public config and outbound authorization semantics in an area previously classified as product hardening, so automation should not choose the trust boundary or compatibility behavior.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in policy
options.body: Define a new outbound recipient allowlist that leaves existing sends unchanged unless configured, then implement schema, docs, logging, and tests.

options.title: Keep as not planned
options.body: Close the feature direction and keep the trusted-operator model plus existing message action/cross-context controls as the supported boundary.

options.title: Use inbound allowFrom
options.body: Treat inbound sender allowlists as outbound recipient allowlists too, accepting the docs and compatibility break this would create.

recommendation.title: Add explicit opt-in policy
recommendation.body: Define a new outbound recipient allowlist that leaves existing sends unchanged unless configured, then implement schema, docs, logging, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior outbound allowlist security triage and adjacent security/outbound policy history make this the best available product/security routing owner.
